subject: Request: Conditional Discount while per-route billing lands
messages:
From: Jordan Ellis <jordan.ellis@acmecorp.com>
To: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 15 Mar 2026 08:14:00 -0500
Subject: Re: Evaluation + pricing for Q2 rollout

Hi Rishi / Monica,

Thanks again for the demo last week — overall the platform looks promising. Two points that are blocking procurement approval on our side: per-route token-level billing (so our finance team can map spend to product lines) and a firm GA date for a streaming stability fix we need for long chat sessions.

Procurement is pushing for either a credit or an upfront discount to bridge the gap while these features land. They want something that limits our vendor risk if timelines slip. We’re launching a pilot the first week of April and need a commercial plan in place this week to get procurement signature.

Would Redwood be able to provide a temporary concession (credit or discount) tied to a roadmap commitment? If so, what would the terms look like and who do we need to sign off internally?

Best,
Jordan Ellis
Head of Platform Ops, ACME Corp

---

Cc: Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 15 Mar 2026 09:02:00 -05:00
Subject: FWD: ACME request — discount tied to roadmap commitment (need approvals)

Team,

ACME is asking for a temporary commercial concession while two items land:
- per-route token-level billing (billing metadata) — blocker for their chargeback
- streaming stability fix for long chat sessions (affects pilot success)

They want a discount/credit that is conditional on us delivering the features within an agreed window. Pilot starts first week of April and procurement wants a signed commercial note this week.

Proposed commercial options to discuss quickly:
- Option A: 30% off list for 6 months, auto-revoked if feature GA delayed beyond 60 days past committed date
- Option B: One-time credit that equals 3 months expected spend, applied if features are not GA by agreed milestone
- Option C: 20% off for 4 months if we provide a written roadmap commitment + acceptance criteria and a short SLA addendum for pilot availability

Ask: Laura / Dev / Monica — what’s feasible from product, legal, and finance? I’ve attached the customer MAP for context. We need a final answer and any suggested wording for the credit/discount by EOD today so I can loop ACME.

Thanks —
Rishi Malhotra
Sr. Account Executive, Redwood Inference

Date: Mon, 16 Mar 2026 10:18:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: FWD: ACME request — discount tied to roadmap commitment (need approvals)

Rishi / all,

Quick product note on timelines and risk: PROD-2498 (per-route billing) is scheduled for an internal release the week of 4/27 with a GA target of 5/11 if no major regressions surface. Streaming stability work is in the same sprint train but carries medium risk — realistic GA window is late-May. We can prioritize the ACME pilot path and try to get a limited-scope billing export earlier (e.g., CSV export of per-route tokens) by mid-April as an interim solution.

I don’t want to promise GA dates in a legally-binding doc given the risk, but we can provide:
- A written roadmap commitment that includes target dates and acceptance criteria (logs + per-route report sample)
- A pilot SLA (1-month pilot availability target, with escalation path)

If the customer needs immediate billing parity for internal chargebacks, the CSV interim is our fastest path.

Given those timelines, I support Option C (20% for 4 months) conditional on:
1) ACME signs the roadmap commitment and agrees to acceptance tests for the pilot;
2) We reserve the right to revoke or convert the concession if ACME requests functionality beyond the agreed acceptance criteria;
3) Finance/legal sign off on credit mechanics.

I’ll link the JIRA and draft the acceptance criteria after this thread.

Laura Bennett
Director, Product Management — Serving Runtime
Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: FWD: ACME request — discount tied to roadmap commitment (need approvals)

Finance/legal have reviewed. Summary of approved terms:
- Approved concession: 20% discount off committed invoices for first 4 billing cycles following production pilot start, not to exceed $120k total.
- Conditionality: Discount only applies if ACME signs the roadmap commitment and accepts pilot acceptance criteria. If GA slips beyond 6/01/2026, discount is subject to review.
- Mechanics: One-time credit note issued to ACME within 30 days of pilot start (credit applied to invoices). Credit note template attached.
- Legal: We will not amend the main MSA; instead we will attach a short Commercial Addendum (defines roadmap, acceptance tests, credit mechanics). Addendum must be signed by customer and Redwood Sales leader.

Markus has given conditional exec approval for this approach; Priya will coordinate the commercial addendum and DocuSign workflow.

Please confirm that Rishi will present Option C terms to Jordan today and attach the roadmap commitment + addendum for signature.

Thanks,
Dev Patel
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference
dev_patel@redwood.com

Jordan / Aisha,

Thanks for the patience — we can offer the following commercial concession tied to the roadmap commitment:

- 20% off committed invoices for the first 4 billing cycles after your production pilot starts (not to exceed $120,000 in aggregate).
- Conditions: ACME signs the attached Roadmap Commitment and Commercial Addendum which define target dates and the pilot acceptance tests (we will provide CSV per-route reporting as an interim during the pilot).
- Mechanics: Redwood will issue a one-time credit note that will be applied to your invoices within 30 days of pilot start.
- If GA for per-route billing slips beyond 2026-06-01, we will re-evaluate the concession in good faith.

I’ve attached the Roadmap Commitment and the Commercial Addendum for signature via DocuSign. Dev / Priya will manage the DocuSign flow; Monica will coordinate credit note issuance with billing once pilot start is confirmed.

If this sounds OK, I can send the DocuSign package now and we’ll target signature by EOD to meet your procurement timeline.
